title: Proximity over pay: Why small towns attract migrants
summary: Because rural migrants are deterred far more by distance than they are drawn by higher pay, nearby towns – despite offering lower earnings than cities – end up absorbing far more migrants and doing more to reduce poverty, making them a decisive channel for inclusive urban growth.

title: Who answers a survey changes how much we think people earn
summary: When relatives answer on someone else’s behalf, men’s earnings are reported too low. In Mexico, this makes the measured gender wage gap 25% narrower.

title: Will open source AI keep up for long?
summary: Open source AI is likely further behind closed-source than current benchmarks indicate. If this gap grows, which is certainly possible, it would limit the usefulness of open source AI across a broad spectrum of capabilities that will be important for LMICs.

title: What are open source AI models and why do they matter for development?
summary: What are the strengths of open source AI? How do you compare different AI models? And how is access to the frontier bought?

title: Lockdowns, domestic violence, and the decline in reporting
summary: Chile’s staggered lockdowns raised helpline calls and shelter use, but not police reports. Cash transfers mitigated the effect.

title: Cape Town's day zero: How a water crisis built a data-driven city
summary: A decade after Cape Town came within days of running dry, a senior city policy official reflects on how the 'day zero' drought reshaped the way the city collects, shares, and acts on data.

title: How BRAC partners with governments to fight poverty at scale
summary: Stephanie Brockerhoff on reaching the poorest of the poor, how BRAC works with government, and what it takes to deliver graduation programmes at scale

title: How decision fatigue undermines diversity in grant-making
summary: In an Ethiopian business plan competition, judges voted less for strong female candidates over the course of repeated assessments, but a simple reminder of the organisation’s commitment to equal opportunity offset this decline.

title: Mining for peace: Why and how the location of new mines shapes conflict risk
summary: Whether a new mine raises or lowers a country's risk of violence depends not only on the mine itself, but on the country's entire ethnic and mining geography. Results for Sierra Leone and sub-Saharan Africa suggests that some deposits can be mined for peace.

title: How admission to a top university reshapes a family's future
summary: In Chile, elite universities reproduce privilege, but for outsiders who get in, they also open a real path to the very top across generations.

title: Gains and trade-offs from government demand
summary: In Uganda, winning government contracts raises firms' total sales, but largely by reallocating supply away from private customers rather than generating net new business, with no gains in productivity or wages.
